description: Implement secure multi-user management with bearer-token auth, per-user data isolation, set-user UI flows, and CLI --user support.

userStories.title: Add users persistence model and store
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a dedicated users store so user identity and token verifier data can be persisted safely.
acceptanceCriteria: Add users.json storage with deterministic schema including email, name, token hash verifier metadata, and schema version.
users.json default path is ~/.mealplan/users.json with env override.
Canonical users-store env var is MEALPLAN_USERS_STORE_PATH.
Store never persists plaintext bearer tokens.
Target file mode is 0600; if weaker permissions are detected, continue and write warning to logger mealplan.security.

userStories.title: Implement token generation, hashing, and verification utilities
userStories.description: As a developer, I want hardened token utilities so issued tokens are unguessable and safely verifiable.
acceptanceCriteria: Token generation uses secrets.token_urlsafe(32) and format mpu_v1_<token>.
Hashing uses Argon2id with defaults: memory_cost=65536 KiB, time_cost=3, parallelism=1, hash_len=32.
Hash verifier includes algorithm/version metadata.
Verification is constant-time and supports rehash recommendation when stored params are weaker than current defaults.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Define auth and set-user API contracts
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want explicit request/response contracts so integrations are deterministic.
acceptanceCriteria: Add contracts for register user, attach existing token, and exchange token.
Route contracts are fixed to POST /api/v1/users/register, POST /api/v1/users/attach-token, and POST /api/v1/users/exchange-token.
Add and confirm canonical error envelope usage for auth and user-management failures.
Implement auth error defaults: 401 auth_missing_token, 401 auth_invalid_token, 403 auth_token_email_mismatch, 409 user_already_exists, 429 auth_rate_limited.
429 responses include Retry-After: 60.

userStories.title: Implement email canonicalization and filename mapping
userStories.description: As a developer, I want deterministic email normalization and filename mapping so user-partitioned files are filesystem-safe.
acceptanceCriteria: Email identity canonicalization order is trim then lowercase.
Filename mapping replaces every char not in [a-zA-Z0-9.] with underscore.

userStories.description: As a user, I want protected APIs to require a valid bearer token so only authorized users can access their data.
acceptanceCriteria: Protected routes reject missing, invalid, or unknown bearer tokens with canonical auth errors.

userStories.title: Implement brute-force protection for bearer-protected APIs
userStories.description: As an operator, I want baseline abuse protection so repeated auth attempts are rate-limited.
acceptanceCriteria: Rate limit applies to all bearer-protected API endpoints.
Keying is per IP and endpoint pair.
Threshold is 100 requests per minute per IP+endpoint.
Breach returns 429 auth_rate_limited and Retry-After: 60.
Cooldown is enforced for 1 minute per offending key.
Client-IP source defaults to socket remote address and X-Forwarded-For is trusted only for configured trusted proxy CIDR(s).
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Add set-user API endpoints register attach exchange
userStories.description: As a web client, I want dedicated user-management endpoints so account bootstrap and token lifecycle are explicit.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/v1/users/register creates new user only if email not already registered; duplicate returns 409 user_already_exists.
Register response returns plaintext token once while persisting only hashed verifier.
POST /api/v1/users/attach-token validates email and token pairing; mismatch returns 403 auth_token_email_mismatch.
POST /api/v1/users/exchange-token validates existing token and returns newly issued token.
Exchange operation is atomic and old token becomes invalid immediately after success.
User/token mutation writes use safe atomic persistence: file lock, temp file write, fsync, and atomic rename.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

acceptanceCriteria: Calendar and food-log API handlers derive user from bearer token and resolve <user-prefix>-calendar.json and <user-prefix>-food-log.json.
Authenticated users cannot read or write another user's files through API calls.
